examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: with a past-tense verb: я бы подумал = I would think
wishes: купили бы = we could have bought

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?
She's offended. She's always like that.

examples.text: А где машинка? Где моя машинка?
examples.trans: Hey, where's the toy car? Where's my toy car?

related.gloss: to reach, walk as far as

meanings.note: affectionate form of дочь; also used by older people to address a young woman

examples.text: Мой Гриша мечтать об этом не мог! Спасибо, дочка!
examples.trans: My Grisha could not even dream of this! Thank you, dear!

meanings.note: in threats: ты ещё увидишь = you'll see

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.en: to jam, to get stuck, to seize up
meanings.note: Often impersonal: дверь заклинило. Colloquially of a person: to freeze up, get fixated (его заклинило).

examples.trans: Chef, Lyova's frozen up on us.
Understood. And who is managing the dining room?

meanings.note: verb: Что это значит? = What does it mean?
мне кажется = I think, it seems to me

examples.trans: I think I've seen you somewhere.

meanings.note: in exclamations: какой грязный! = how dirty!

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!
I love our town very much.
You're in love with another man's wife!

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

examples.text: Это неправда! Вы у меня записаны как Батя.
examples.trans: That's not true! I have you saved as 'Dad'.

meanings.note: usually in the genitive ничего, with не: ничего не осталось

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: accusative/genitive его (него after prepositions), dative ему (нему)

meanings.en: other forms: его (gen/acc), ему (dat), им (instr), нём (prep)

examples.text: Она нашла нас на новом месте.
examples.trans: She found us at the new place.
That is it, she got really offended.
She is not answering her phone.
I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: declines like a feminine noun in -а, but is masculine

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

examples.text: Подожди, Нин, ты не поняла. Это же стыдно!
examples.trans: Wait, Nina, you don't get it. It's shameful!
Do you remember the toilet in the communal flat?

порадоваться.gloss: to rejoice, to be happy, to be glad

examples.trans: So she would be happy for you!

examples.text: Чтобы она за тебя порадовалась! И меня простила.
examples.trans: So she'd be happy for you! And forgive me.

meanings.note: работать + instrumental = to work as: работать мэром

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been working as mayor for four years now.
Wait, what, Lyova is a robot?
This robot washes the dishes by itself.
We'll definitely have a big wedding!

examples.text: Макс, зачем ты соврал про нашу будущую свадьбу?
examples.trans: Max, why did you lie about our future wedding?
Then a wedding, and then kids!

meanings.note: refers back to the subject: 'он держит своё слово' = he keeps his word

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

examples.text: Виктор Степанович, сегодня никак не могу.
examples.trans: Viktor Stepanovich, I really can't today.
The wind is blowing hard outside.

examples.text: Я так два года потеряла. Любила так сильно!
examples.trans: I lost two years like that. I loved him so much!

meanings.note: once; что скажешь? = what do you say?

examples.trans: Tell us, when will your programme be out?

meanings.en: to be able to, to manage to

examples.trans: We came as soon as we could.
Will you be able to come tomorrow morning?

examples.text: Я думаю, что у меня есть мужчина. Он сможет меня защитить.
examples.trans: I think that I have a man. He will be able to protect me.

examples.text: Я совсем не это хочу сказать.
examples.trans: That's not what I mean at all.

examples.text: Нет, Вика, я совсем не это хочу сказать.
examples.trans: No, Vika, that's not what I mean at all.

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: the plural is a different word: люди, людям, о людях

examples.trans: There are a lot of people here.
I know the problems of ordinary people.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Informal. Borrowed from French 'chef' (head, leader, from Latin 'caput'); in Russian kitchen culture 'шеф' is the standard form of address for the executive head chef.

examples.trans: The chef is in the kitchen.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
